newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka calls for laws to curb computer crime.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka calls for laws to curb computer crime.

text.p: A Sri Lankan government committee has called for laws to curb rising computer crime, the state-owned Daily News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said there were instances of computer fraud in Sri Lanka but most were not reported to police as they were not covered by the penal code.
It quoted Deputy Solicitor General Kolitha Dharmawardena as saying that people who stole computers or defrauded customers during sale of the machines could be charged in a court of law.
"(But) if someone meddles with information served by a computer, reporting to police will be of no avail. There is no law under which police can take action," Dharmawardena said.
The newspaper said some institutions were conducting internal inquiries into computer-related crimes as they did not want interference from police not trained to investigate such offences.
It did not give specific instances.

The committee, which comprised officials from police and customs department and the Computer and Information Technology Council of Sri Lanka (CINTEC) among others, has recommended severe punishments, including heavy fines and imprisonment, to deter people from committing computer-related offences.
